bib.title: EVA: Exploring the Limits of Masked Visual Representation Learning at Scale

question: Can masked image modeling with image-text aligned (CLIP) feature targets scale a vanilla ViT to one billion parameters on public data and transfer to many vision tasks and to CLIP training?
hypothesis: Regressing masked-out CLIP vision features scales well and gives strong transfer without a supervised pre-training stage.
contributions: EVA, a 1.0B vanilla ViT pre-trained by masked CLIP-feature regression on 29.6M public images
New records on ImageNet-1K, Kinetics, COCO, LVISv1.0, COCO-Stuff and ADE20K as reported
EVA as vision tower initialisation stabilises and accelerates a 1.1B CLIP (EVA CLIP-g)
Release of code and billion-scale models

method.summary: A 40-layer ViT-g is pre-trained to reconstruct OpenAI CLIP-L/14 vision features of 40% block-masked patches with negative cosine loss on 29.6M public images for 150 epochs. It is then fine-tuned per task (classification, video, detection, segmentation) and used to initialise the vision tower of a 1.1B CLIP trained on LAION-400M.
method.task: masked image modeling pre-training with transfer evaluation; CLIP zero-shot classification

datasets.name: Pre-training merge: ImageNet-21K, CC12M, CC3M, Object365, COCO, ADE20K
datasets.split: COCO and ADE20K train sets only; CC12M/CC3M images without captions

datasets.name: ImageNet-21K (intermediate fine-tune) / ImageNet-1K
datasets.split: IN-21K 60 epochs at 224px then IN-1K 10 epochs (336px) or 15 (560px); eval on IN-1K val

datasets.name: Kinetics-722 (K-400+K-600+K-700 merged, de-duplicated)
datasets.split: leaked/repeated videos removed by youtube id

datasets.name: Objects365, COCO, LVISv1.0
datasets.split: O365 intermediate then COCO / LVIS train

other.pretraining_note: no relative pos emb or layer-scale

models.name: EVA CLIP-g
models.init_from: vision: pre-trained EVA; text: OpenAI CLIP-L

models.name: Open CLIP-H, Open CLIP-g, ALIGN, OpenAI CLIP-L

training.objective: regress masked CLIP-L/14 vision features; EVA output normalised then linear-projected; negative cosine similarity loss; block-wise masking ratio 40%
training.optimizer: AdamW (Adam with decoupled weight decay 0.05), betas (0.9, 0.98)
training.compute: ~14.5 pt days on 128 GPUs; ~3150 samples/sec; ~26.5GB max mem

other.downstream_finetune: IN-21K: lr 1e-4, bs 4096, 60 ep, warmup 15, layer decay 0.85, drop path 0.4 (Table 12); IN-1K: lr 3e-5, bs 512, 10/15 ep, ema 0.9999, label smoothing 0.3 (Table 13)
other.detection: O365 380k iters bs 128 lr 1e-4; COCO 45k / LVIS 75k steps bs 64 lr 2.5e-5, 1280px (Tables 17-18)
other.clip_training: EVA CLIP-g: batch 41k, 256x A100 40GB, fp16, Open CLIP codebase + DeepSpeed ZeRO-1; lr, steps, optimizer not stated

inference.samples: single run per number; no seeds reported

parameters.detection_tta: multi-scale test-time augmentation and Soft-NMS for COCO; single-scale also reported

metrics.name: top-1 accuracy
metrics.definition: ImageNet-1K val, Kinetics, and zero-shot classification

metrics.name: AP box / AP mask
metrics.definition: COCO and LVISv1.0 detection and instance segmentation

metrics.name: mIoU
metrics.definition: ADE20K and COCO-Stuff, single-scale (ss) and multi-scale (ms)

eval.protocol: single run, no seeds or significance tests; comparisons against numbers from other papers (timestamp Nov 10, 2022)

limits: Teacher is OpenAI CLIP-L trained on 400M image-text pairs, so public-data-only is conditional (authors concede)
Segmentation architecture weakened for GPU memory; ADE20K below BEiT-3
Zero LVIS-COCO mask gap is not a solved large vocabulary task; rare AP 48.3 vs frequent 57.4
Single runs, no seeds; comparisons use competitor numbers as of Nov 10, 2022
EVA CLIP optimizer, lr and steps not stated
Text/table inconsistencies: zero-shot 78.2 vs 78.5; avg 72.7 vs 75.7; samples seen 11B vs 7B

lineage.note: MIM family; BEiT-3 is main competitor
pretext task not originally proposed here

figures.caption: An illustration of this work. We find with sufficient image data (30M) and compute (150 epochs), simply regressing the masked out image-text aligned vision features (i.e., CLIP features) scales up well
EVA as a vision-centric, multi-modal pivot
